label: Publish
tagline: Take a prototype live on the internet using the user's own GitHub + Supabase
description: Publishes a Woven prototype to a real public URL using the USER'S OWN accounts (never Woven's). API / GitHub-app first: creates a GitHub repo under the signed-in account, exports the prototype source, pushes, enables a static host (GitHub Pages for the MVP), and returns the live URL. For the simple-DB path it then provisions a Supabase project (profiles / preferences / files), injects the client config, and redeploys. Detects whether GitHub is linked and, if not, emits a link-GitHub task instead of failing. Lets the user pick a domain target (default github.io / a free getwoven.design subdomain / their own custom domain) and a setup style: AUTOMATIC (the agent does it for you server-side, API-first with browser-use fallback, planning + confirming before each irreversible step) or GUIDED (the agent gives click-by-click steps and the user performs each one). No separate dry-run flag - safety is the plan-then-confirm in AUTOMATIC and the user-drives nature of GUIDED. Detects existing state (already-connected repo / prior publish.json) and updates rather than duplicating. MVP scope = the simple-website / simple-DB path only; the complex-app classifier + flow/data-object breakdown + two-agent grill loop are deferred. Writes durable state to <project>/publish.json (the seed of the development-task surface). Honors the no-terminal-for-user rule: in AUTOMATIC the agent does the work; in GUIDED it hands the user click-by-click steps, and only because they chose it.

triggers.title: publish / deploy / take it live
triggers.rule: User wants the current prototype put online (publish, deploy, ship it, take it live, put it on the internet, give me a real URL, host it). Dispatch publish-orchestrator. It gates on GitHub being linked, detects whether the project was already published (and updates rather than duplicating), honors the chosen setup style (automatic / guided) + domain target, runs M1 (static deploy) and, when the user wants stored profiles/preferences/files, M2 (Supabase). It uses the USER'S accounts via the stored GitHub token + a Supabase token the user connects - never Woven's infra.

hardRule.body: When the user asks to PUBLISH / DEPLOY / take a prototype live / put it on the internet / get a real shareable URL that is NOT the ephemeral getwoven.design share tunnel, dispatch the `publish-orchestrator` (Task subagent_type: publish-orchestrator). Do NOT attempt the GitHub repo creation, push, host enablement, or Supabase provisioning inline yourself - the orchestrator owns the cost-warning, the setup style (automatic / guided), the domain target, the GitHub-linked + existing-state detection, and the durable publish.json state machine. Publishing uses the USER'S OWN GitHub + Supabase accounts, never Woven's broker/tunnel infra (that is only for previews).
